_comment: Ground truth for all Swarm marketing copy. Maintainers only: contributions cannot change this file. Copy may state a number, a forbidden-list topic or an external link only if it is listed here.

facts.claim: The agent runs on the volunteer's own machine, through the official Claude Code or Codex CLI, under the volunteer's own login.
Swarm never reads, stores or transmits subscription credentials or tokens. It only starts the unmodified official CLI.
With the Claude runner the agent has no shell, no web access and no MCP servers; it can only read and edit files in a fresh clone.
Verify commands run in an OS sandbox with no network, a scrubbed environment and no view of the home directory.
The macOS sandbox is tested. Linux (bubblewrap) and Docker modes are implemented but not yet tested by the maintainers.
Every submission carries an ed25519-signed receipt recording task, base commit, tree hash, agent, usage and verify results.
CI re-runs verification using the rules from the base branch, so a submission cannot bring its own rules.

Merging needs an independent signed review from a different worker than the submitter. An agent can do the re-testing, the review and the merge, so no person has to be in the loop; a maintainer can step in at any point.
By default Swarm leaves 20% of the weekly and 5-hour windows untouched and caps each agent run at $3 API-equivalent.
Coordination is git and GitHub pull requests. There is no Swarm server and no peer-to-peer network.
Volunteers choose which projects their quota goes to. Nobody can send a volunteer's agent a task; only maintainers of a chosen project can, by merging a task file.
A pull request is opened only after verification passed on the volunteer's machine. Claims and failed attempts are signed comments on one issue per task.
Swarm is three steps: install the plugin, choose a project, and leftover quota does tasks that project's maintainers wrote.

It runs in Claude Code on the user's computer (tested) and is built to run in Claude Code cloud sessions and scheduled tasks (not yet run in a real one). Installs for Cowork, Codex and Hermes are documented but not yet tested by the maintainers.
On the user's computer Swarm reads the quota windows and keeps a reserve. In a cloud session it cannot, so leftover there means a run scheduled shortly before the weekly reset.
Only repositories whose maintainers added a .swarm directory receive work, and only tasks the maintainers merged are executed.
The CLI has zero npm dependencies and needs Node 20 or newer.
The Claude Code runner is tested end to end. The Codex runner is experimental.
MIT licensed.
Running the official CLI on your own machine under your own login is permitted today; providers can change plan terms, and Swarm is not affiliated with Anthropic or OpenAI.

forbidden.why: Coordination is git and GitHub, not a P2P network. Say so only to deny it, inside a line containing 'not' or 'no'.
Nothing is pooled. Tokens never leave the volunteer's machine.
Verification reduces risk; it guarantees nothing.
